title: Phase 1 CPU Micro-Scale 7-Arm Proof-of-Life & Diagnostic Validation
scale: micro-small (0.98M) vs micro-large (2.85M), 80 sup + 20 RL steps, 600 train / 64 Reg1 + 48 Reg3 eval, seed=42
hardware: AMD Ryzen 5 7430U (12 logical CPUs, 62 GiB RAM, CPU-only)
bugs_caught: I2-Hybrid train-vs-eval interface mismatch in phase1_pilot/eval/diagnostics.py (prepended 4 pure continuous latents + <think>/</think> delimiters during eval despite rollout_hybrid using thought_len blended steps directly, causing fake NLL=7.68, Hard-BPB=5.030, ECE=0.844, 4.71x FLOPs; fixed to <1e-4 parity with recompute_hybrid_logprobs_and_continuation and locked with regression test).

Missing torch.distributed init/broadcast/sharding/grad all-reduce in train.py and grpo.py when launched under multi-GPU torchrun (fixed and verified with 2-rank Gloo test) + missing rl/__init__.py exports.
lessons: Binary exact-match R1 (RL-R1) suffers 100% zero-variance starvation (sigma_zero_frac=1.00) on low-accuracy small models, whereas strictly proper Brier R3 (RL-R3, I2-Hybrid) maintains sigma_zero_frac=0.00 with bounded no-thought drift.

I2-Hybrid is the strongest small-model arm (Hard-BPB 2.271 vs B2 2.266, OOD pass@16 37.5% vs B1/B2/B3 31.2%, delta_nll_trunc=+2.732 nats), but running thought_len=6 on every target token yields 2.51x B2 FLOPs; Stage 1 needs sparse/adaptive inference triggering to hit <=1.0x B2 FLOPs.

At 0.98M params and 80+20 steps, delta_nll_swap remains ~0.000 across all arms even when delta_nll_trunc is strongly positive (+2.73 to +2.91 nats), confirming micro-scale validates pipeline invariants but cannot decide H1b.

title: Regime 1 learnability scoping: no micro NTP model leaves the structural floor (EXP-001 reinterpreted)
scale: 13 single-model probes (B1 micro-small, one B2 micro-large), 50k-sample train sets, batch 32, 3k-20k supervised steps; no RL, no thought arms; not preregistered (scoping)
bugs_caught: Pointer variables v16-v31 tokenize as two PilotTokenizer tokens whose first is itself a variable name; probe default pool cut to v0-v15 (--pool-size 32 reproduces the first probes)

modular_varbind eval_id d=1 cells leak: 7/200 (trained on d=1) and 1/67 (trained on d=1,2,3) eval prompts equal a train prompt up to equation order, because split dedup compares rendered prompts; no overlap found at d=2,4 or in pointer chains
lessons: EXP-001's Regime 1 arms all score worse than the prompt-blind reference (NLL 3.362-3.452 vs 3.150), so its Hard-BPB, pass@k and Delta-NLL comparisons are uninformative about reasoning in either direction (DE-007).
Only 1 of 89 cells beats its structural floor after Bonferroni correction: python_trace d=1 trained on d=1 alone (17.0% vs 6.0%, n=200).

Single lookups (3 key-value pairs, single-token names, answer-only loss) stay at 31-36% for 20k steps (copy floor 1/3); answer NLL settles near ln 3 (1.12-1.14), consistent with spreading mass over the three listed literals. The mechanism is not identified: no candidate-mass or key-swap probe was run.
LlamaLM matches transformers' LlamaForCausalLM logits exactly with copied weights, so the backbone forward pass is not the cause (tests/test_llama_reference.py).
compute_hours sums each probe's own training time; probes ran 2-4 at a time.
Gate EXP-002 on base-model competence: B1 must beat the structural floor on ID Regime 1 before any arm comparison is read; otherwise the verdict is INCONCLUSIVE.

title: Trainer check on Zoology MQAR (BL-12 step 1): micro-small LlamaLM + train_supervised learns MQAR; one label per row fits train rows but not held-out
scale: 3 arms (micro-small, 0.92M / 0.86M), 10k-row MQAR train sets, batch 32, 10k supervised steps, seed 42; preregistered (commit 6180c3a); Part A probes an EXP-006 checkpoint
lessons: Rule A: M1 (Zoology basic MQAR, 4 labelled queries per row) reaches test accuracy 1.000 (first >= 0.99 at step 3,500) with default train_supervised settings, so a general trainer or backbone defect is unlikely to explain the EXP-006 single-lookup plateau.

M2 (same inputs, 1 labelled query per row) fits its training batches (last batch: all 32 labels right, loss 2.3e-4) while held-out accuracy stays 0.12-0.20 at every eval, below the 1/K = 0.25 copy floor; likely memorization (train-set accuracy not measured). One label per row confounds answers per step with distinct supervised answers (10k vs 40k).
M3 (16 keys, 19 values, K=3, all queries labelled) reaches 0.995 at step 1,000 and 1.000 from step 4,500: the combined small setting is learnable under dense supervision.

Part A: the EXP-006 20k-step pointer model puts 99.3-99.5% of its mass on the three listed literals, but its greedy answer changes with the queried key in only 3-5.5% of prompts; it copies a literal without key matching.

Budget estimate was wrong: about 80 min wall clock per arm vs 25 min preregistered (3.95 elapsed arm-hours summed over concurrent arms vs under 1.5); the per-step time came from a solo run, and host load was about 20 on 12 threads.

Next: BL-12 step 2 (to be preregistered): MQAR one-query 2x2 of batch {32,128} x rows {10k,40k}; pointer d=0 with identical all-heads inputs and 1 vs 3 answer labels, a rerun one-query control, batch 128, and a fresh holdout.
